title: The Baby and the Stone

panels.visual: Uranus the starry Sky, a vast face made of night and stars, stretched over Gaia the Earth, a giant mountain-woman with a stern face; tiny lightning
panels.caption: Before the gods there were the Titans. Their father was Uranus, the Sky. He was cruel to his children.

panels.visual: Cronus, a huge wild-haired Titan with burning eyes, gripping a giant curved stone sickle, leaping up at the sky in a dark storm
panels.caption: His son Cronus took a giant sickle and attacked his father.

panels.visual: Dark-red drops of blood falling from the torn night sky onto the earth like a storm of red rain, Cronus seen small below, sickle raised
panels.caption: Drops of the Sky's blood rained down on the Earth.

panels.visual: Out of red puddles in the earth rise the Furies, three snake-haired winged women with glowing eyes, and huge armoured Giants climbing out of the ground, horror lighting
panels.caption: Where they fell, monsters sprang up: the Furies and the Giants.

panels.visual: Old Gaia, the Earth, whispering a prophecy into Cronus's ear, his eyes widening in fear, dark background with a cracked crown
panels.caption: Then Cronus was warned: one of your children will overthrow you.

speech.speaker: Gaia
speech.text: Your own child will take your throne.

panels.visual: Horror shot from below: the giant Cronus towering in a dark palace, wild bulging eyes, cheeks puffed out as he gulps something down, a small empty cradle in the foreground, his wife Rhea in the background with her hands over her face in despair
panels.caption: So every time his wife Rhea had a baby, he swallowed it whole.

panels.visual: Five small glowing ghost-like silhouettes of children (Hestia, Demeter, Hera, Hades, Poseidon) waiting together in a gloomy dark cave-like space, worried but alive, faint red light
panels.caption: Hestia, Demeter, Hera, Hades, Poseidon. Five children, alive in their father's belly.

panels.visual: A museum wall in the Prado with a dark, rough old oil painting in a gold frame showing a wild grey-haired giant with mad staring white eyes in blackness, dark red smears; a small modern girl visitor stepping back in shock
panels.caption: Two thousand years later the painter Goya painted it even worse: Cronus chewing.

panels.visual: Rhea in a dark cave handing Cronus a heavy stone wrapped in baby blankets, her face hiding a secret smile, Cronus snatching it greedily
panels.caption: When the sixth baby came, Rhea wrapped a stone in baby clothes.

panels.visual: Cronus gulping the wrapped stone down whole, throat bulging; inset, baby Zeus safe in a cave on Crete with a goat, and warriors banging their shields to hide his crying
panels.caption: Cronus gulped it down. Baby Zeus grew up in secret on Crete.

panels.visual: Grown-up Zeus, young and strong with a thunderbolt, as Cronus doubles over and spews out a big stone and five grown gods tumbling out alive in a disgusting gush
panels.caption: Grown up, Zeus made him throw up the stone and all five children, alive.

panels.visual: Zeus and his brothers and sisters standing together in lightning against the defeated Titans, Cronus chained in the dark depths below; in the corner, a round carved stone on an altar at Delphi
panels.caption: Together they beat the Titans. The Greeks said the stone itself was kept at Delphi.

mood: Gothic horror mood for this story: deep black shadows, a monstrous giant, terrified faces, dripping dark-red ink as the single accent colour; blood shown as falling drops and splashes, never wounds or body parts; frightening but suitable for brave children aged 9 to 11.
